title: Starc and Rahul Fire Delhi Capitals Past Rajasthan Royals to Keep Playoff Hopes Alive
excerpt: Mitchell Starc's devastating three-in-four-balls spell and KL Rahul's record-breaking fifty propel DC to a crucial five-wicket win at the Arun Jaitley Stadium
body:
## A Night of Records and Reckoning in Delhi

Delhi Capitals needed a statement, and they got one. Chasing 194 under the lights at the Arun Jaitley Stadium on May 17, the hosts rode a scintillating fifty from KL Rahul and a clinical death-overs assault from Ashutosh Sharma to overhaul Rajasthan Royals' 193 for 8 with four balls to spare. The five-wicket victory hauled DC from eighth to seventh in the IPL 2026 standings—still precarious at 12 points, but very much alive.

The evening belonged, in the first instance, to Mitchell Starc. The Australian left-armer, who had endured an indifferent tournament by his own exacting standards, produced a spell of devastating hostility in the middle overs that turned the contest on its head. His figures of 4 for 40 included three wickets in four deliveries—agonisingly close to a hat-trick—that triggered a remarkable Rajasthan collapse from 161 for 2 to 193 for 8. It was a passage of play that reminded onlookers why Delhi paid a record sum for him two seasons ago.

## Rajasthan's Promise, Then Implosion

Rajasthan had looked supremely placed at the halfway mark of their innings. Dhruv Jurel, batting with a maturity that belied his 24 years, anchored the top order with a composed 53, while captain Riyan Parag—returning from a brief absence—struck 51 in his characteristically audacious fashion. The pair added momentum that Vaibhav Sooryavanshi then supercharged with a blistering 46 off just 21 balls, including four sixes that sailed deep into the Delhi night.

Yet from that position of plenty, Rajasthan lost six wickets for a mere 32 runs. Starc was the chief architect, but Delhi's bowling unit operated as a collective. The collapse underscored a recurring vulnerability: when their middle order is tested under pressure, RR's batting can unravel with startling speed. They remain on 12 points but slipped in the standings, their own playoff arithmetic now distinctly less comfortable.

Notably, Ravindra Jadeja was absent from Rajasthan's XI, rested as part of workload management ahead of the business end of the season. His all-round presence—both with the ball in the middle overs and with the bat in the lower order—was conspicuously missed.

## Rahul Rewrites the Record Books

DC captain Rahul won the toss and chose to bowl, a decision vindicated by Starc's heroics. When it was Delhi's turn to bat, Rahul led from the front. His 56, compiled with the unhurried elegance that has become his trademark, provided the foundation for the chase. It was his 50th IPL fifty—a milestone that places him among the tournament's all-time greats—and, more remarkably, his ninth score of 50 or more against Rajasthan Royals in just 19 innings, surpassing AB de Villiers' long-standing record of eight.

Abishek Porel complemented Rahul with a brisk 51, and when the asking rate climbed in the final overs, Axar Patel's unbeaten 34 and Ashutosh Sharma's explosive cameo of 18 off just five balls sealed the deal. Starc, fittingly, was named Player of the Match.

## The Diaspora Watches, and Hopes

For the millions of Indian cricket fans scattered across time zones from San Jose to Singapore, DC's do-or-die scenario has become appointment viewing on JioHotstar. KL Rahul, whose polished batting and composed demeanour have earned him a vast following among NRI audiences, delivered precisely when it mattered most. Social media lit up across diaspora hubs—WhatsApp groups in the Bay Area, watch parties in London pubs, late-night streams in Melbourne living rooms—as Sharma's final boundary cleared the ropes.

The IPL's ability to command global attention during the Indian evening is, by now, well-documented. But it is matches like these—taut, dramatic, decided in the final overs—that transform casual viewers into committed fans abroad. For NRIs who grew up watching Rahul's career unfold, his record-breaking knock carried an emotional weight that transcended mere statistics.

## What Lies Ahead

Delhi's path to the playoffs remains treacherous. At 12 points with results still to come, they likely need to win their remaining matches and hope other results fall favourably. Rajasthan, equally, cannot afford complacency. The bottom half of the table is separated by margins so thin that a single net run rate swing could alter the picture entirely.

The next fixture pits Chennai Super Kings against Sunrisers Hyderabad on May 18 at the MA Chidambaram Stadium—another contest with significant implications for the playoff race. In a season that has defied prediction at nearly every turn, the only certainty is that more drama awaits.
